newsitem.title: USA: USA: BASEBALL-MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL TO INVESTIGATE CORDERO.
newsitem.headline: USA: BASEBALL-MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL TO INVESTIGATE CORDERO.

text.p: Major League Baseball plans to investigate Boston's Wil Cordero following a report in the Boston Globe newspaper involving the Red Sox outfielder's alleged history of domestic violence.

"Allegations of domestic abuse and domestic violence are to be taken extremely seriously," said acting commissioner Bud Selig. "There is no room in baseball or society for such behaviour and we in baseball abhor it."

Cordero was slated Thursday night to make his first start at home since being charged earlier this month with domestic abuse. He was scratched from the lineup after the team received new information about disturbing incidents dating back to 1990.

Cordero had appeared in just six games for the Red Sox since he was arrested June 11 on charges of battering his second wife, Ana Echevarria. He pleaded innocent to charges of assault with a dangerous weapon and assault and battery and his wife refused to testify against him, although prosecutors are continuing their investigation.

Plans for him to play Thursday night were reversed after a report surfaced in the Globe disclosing past abuse charges against Cordero by his first wife. The accusations, which were included in a court document obtained by the newspaper, claim Cordero beat Wanda Mora Cordero repeatedly, including while she was pregnant.
A pre-game meeting involving Cordero, Red Sox manager Jimy Williams and general manager Dan Duquette lasted into the first inning before the outfielder left the ballpark, escorted by security.

Red Sox attorneys were made aware of Wanda Cordero's charges, the Globe reported. All of the allegations made by Wanda Cordero in the 1993 document occurred while Cordero was with the Montreal Expos organisation.
At the time, Duquette was an executive in the Montreal organisation, and it was Duquette who engineered Boston's acquisition of Cordero just prior to the 1996 season.
But the club denied any knowledge of Cordero's past domestic problems.

"We, the Red Sox, including Dan (Duquette) had no previous knowledge of these allegations, despite any published reports that have come out or will come out," said Red Sox spokesman Kevin Shea. "We knew nothing of the allegations."
The club also released a statement during Thursday's game addressing the latest allegations against Cordero.
"This evening, the Boston Red Sox learned of allegations related to events involving Wil Cordero between 1990 and 1993, before Cordero joined the Red Sox in 1996," the statement said.

"What the Boston Red Sox have been told about the allegations raises new serious issues. Based on this information the Red Sox withdrew Cordero from the lineup. The Red Sox are actively engaging in an expeditious review of this new information."
The 25-year-old Cordero is scheduled for a pre-trial hearing into the June 11 domestic abuse charges on July 24.
